prize_parts.citation: for the prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle in twisted bilayer graphene and the discovery by the Jarillo-Herrero group of correlated insulating and superconducting states, which opened the field of moire quantum materials

statement.case_for: After the full exchange I keep magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene as my single-part position, with MacDonald, Bistritzer and Jarillo-Herrero. The 2011 flat-band prediction and the 2018 observation of correlated insulating and superconducting states form a compact prediction-then-discovery chain, and four members reached the same configuration independently of my own reasoning. What I weigh most, from my own field, is that the phenomenology has now been reproduced by groups using different stacking and fabrication routes, and that twist angle, gating and pressure act as a clean control knob. That is the standard I apply: the prize would go to a reproduced observation, not to an explanation. I have tightened my citation in response to Eriksson's request so that it names the Jarillo-Herrero group as the experimental discovery, which is the honest way to cover Cao and the parallel groups under a three-name limit.
statement.case_against: The pairing mechanism is unresolved, twist-angle disorder and strain still make samples vary, and eight years is short. The credit leaves out Yuan Cao as first author and the parallel observations by Dean, Yacoby, Young and Fatemi, and earlier twisted-bilayer theory by Santos and Peres complicates priority of the prediction. The chair's question about whether these are disqualifying is a fair one. I do not find them disqualifying, but if a majority judged that maturity should govern, B041 or B001 would be the better-seasoned choices and I would not call that an unreasonable result.

responses.point: Pearce argues that B041 is the more mature achievement, with over a decade of confirmation and surpassing in many laboratories, and that B046 has an open pairing question and an uncredited first author.
responses.response: The maturity contrast is real and I take it seriously: the clock record is better seasoned than the moire phenomenology. Where I disagree is on what is being recognised. For B046 the object is the existence of the correlated and superconducting phases at the magic angle, and that has been reproduced widely, so the unresolved mechanism does not weaken the claim. The uncredited first author is the genuine cost, and I propose to handle it in the citation wording rather than pretend it away. I do not move to B041, because I still read it as extending the line honoured in 2005 and 2012. I note that he would not resist B046 if the committee found the weaknesses minor, and I would say the same in reverse.

responses.point: Kroll supports B041 as a clean two-name invention with 1e-18 accuracy, and concedes that a committee weighting breadth of a new field over precision could reasonably choose B046. He also disclosed a link to the Hall laboratory.
responses.response: His own statement of the overlap with the frequency-comb and ion-control prizes is the reason I rank B041 below B046, since a new class of materials is different in kind from a further order of magnitude on a recognised measurement. I accept that the attribution is cleaner than mine, and that matters. His disclosure of the Hall-laboratory link looks like a mentorship connection only, and disclosure seems enough to me, not recusal, but the committee should note it.

responses.point: Eriksson moved to B046 as a prediction-then-discovery chain, noted that B001 is the better-established achievement if maturity governs, and asked that the citation name the Jarillo-Herrero group.
responses.response: I agree with the structure and have adopted his suggestion on the citation. His honest point that B001 would be the safer choice on maturity is the strongest reason I list it as an alternative. I differ on the weight: the theory-led nature of B001 and the Metzner gap he names are, to me, a heavier attribution problem than the uncredited experimentalists on B046, which a citation can partly address.

responses.point: Mehlig keeps dynamical mean-field theory on conceptual originality and over thirty years of confirmation, and admits that Metzner is outside the credited trio and that DMFT may be seen as a method.
responses.response: His durability argument is the best maturity case on the table and I now treat B001 as a real alternative. My difficulty is that, as he says, Metzner is excluded and the method-versus-discovery question is open, so under the three-name limit I cannot see how to repair the credit. I also record that, unlike in my first statement, I now understand his low opening rank of B046 as a maturity judgement, and I would be interested to hear whether the reproducibility across independent groups changes it.

uncertainties: Whether eight years and the open pairing mechanism will weigh enough with colleagues to prefer B041 or B001.
Whether naming the Jarillo-Herrero group in the citation adequately covers Cao and the parallel groups under the three-person limit.
The extent to which the Santos and Peres earlier theory affects priority of the 2011 prediction.
My own judgement of the clock physics is not expert, so I defer to Lindroth and Kroll on the technical weight of B041.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict with any B046 name; my oxide-interface and electron-microscopy work is adjacent to the materials but not connected to the credited people. Göran Johansson is a Chalmers colleague who supports B046 in round 1 and lists B031 as an alternative, which is institutional proximity only. I have no link to the B041 or B001 names that would need disclosure.
